When studying the resurrection of "dead" dino coins... I think Litecoin is the best place to start.

It's experienced more death/resurrection cycles over the years than anything else I've seen before.

Every move followed the same script:
 - breakout from long, slow bleed w/ ascending triangle
 - initial move higher out of the triangle, range right above
 - up only blow off top

Zcash has already experienced the first phase, it looks like it's nearing the end of the second, which means... it's probably about to send a lot higher than most people are ready for.

e.g. in this scenario next clear resistance for ZEC is ~170% higher than where it is right now... in a world where BTC is also climbing back to ATHs and prints another 50% from here while zec outpaces it by 170%, the price of ZEC in USD would hit somewhere around $5K.

I'm going to give a contrarian take on Neoclouds like $NBIS and say the theme looks compelling after the valuation crash. 

Since there's a reason why Elon's $SPCX is heavily focused on this market full of "guppies" that would die: 

He sees how attractive the economics are after selling compute to $GOOGL and Anthropic. 

And this is reflected by his actions not words, from SpaceX's recent $40B financing for GPUs procurement. 
$AMZN, $MSFT, and even $META also see how profitable the economics are and are accelerating their AI DC buildouts. 

I'd argue if a Neocloud has: 

- Close relationships with $NVDA + others for allocations
- Existing contracted capacity + permitting
- Well funded counterparties, such as Hyperscalers. 
- Attractive economics, such as financing their procurement correctly (not the way $CRWV has with high debt interest unless they refinance). 

Then I think they'll do just fine... 

However, the bigger worry is more toward newer players starting financing or the permitting process, since barrier to entry has now become extremely high. 

For financing, read through on $IREN earnings has shown public Neoclouds can adapt extremely well to tight markets:

As seen with their 90% prepayments for GPU capex on a 5Y deal. 

Their older H100 GPUs recontracted at double their previous pricing and 12% higher contracted pricing also point against depreciation fears. 

And in the case DC buildouts slow from permitting delays... it heavily favors some over others. 

Rosenblatt's recent note for example stated they see little risk with $NBIS primary buildout that was in Missouri, Pennsylvania, and South Carolina. 

And there's probably less risk with developers in places like Australia. 

Markets have also show this infinite compute arbitrage can't go on forever, hence the reluctance to further finance capex, via things like ATMs. 

But ironically, tighter financing and hypothetical restrictive permitting would increase the competitive advantage of established neoclouds. 

And create a larger moat against newer DC developers.

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — WEEKEND EDITION | NOV 7 ⚡

The Nasdaq fell 5.5% Thursday after the U.S. midterms. Then Friday’s payrolls came in at +165K vs. +65K expected, sending the dollar and yields higher. Markets ended the week pricing roughly an 80% chance of a December Fed hike.

☢️ URANIUM
TradeTech reported a record $99/lb long-term indicator, with spot near $92 on Friday. Two U.S. utilities signed for 1.1M lb from UEC through 2032 at prevailing spot prices on delivery. On the supply side, Kazatomprom reported Q3 output up 12% year over year on a 100% basis.

🥈 SILVER
Spot jumped 5.7% on the week to $51.94/oz after ending October below $50. Thursday’s interim review is the next test for April’s 46.3M oz deficit forecast.

🟠 COPPER
LME three-month copper fell 3.3% to $13,780/t as the AI trade unwound. Meanwhile, China’s Yangshan import premium hit a record $210/t and Codelco cut its 2026 output outlook to just over 1.2M tonnes. Physical buyers in China are paying up even as futures sell off.

🥇 GOLD
Spot gained 5% on the week to about $4,071/oz despite Friday’s pullback. The World Gold Council reported 321 tonnes of net central-bank buying in Q3, up 42% year over year. Global gold ETFs took in another $2.7B in October.

👀 NEXT WEEK | NOV 9–13

Mon — China CPI and PPI. COP31 opens in Türkiye.
Tue — U.S. CPI, China trade data and NexGen’s Rook I update.
Thu — Metals Focus presents its interim silver findings.
Fri — U.S. PPI.

Tuesday’s CPI is the big test for gold and silver. A softer print could take some pressure off yields. I’m also watching oil after fresh strikes near Hormuz, and whether China’s copper premiums stay elevated if tech stocks slide again.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the next Daily Metals Pulse.

If you’re looking for a year-end trade, look no further.

The $VIX has already spiked to around 27. If it reaches 30, I believe you’ll have the last great trade of the year on your hands.

A $VIX of 30 is not sustainable indefinitely. A market drawdown, by its very nature, reduces the risk of the next drawdown as stocks become cheaper, especially when corporate earnings continue to rise.

Seasonality has played out almost perfectly. And the higher volatility spikes, the faster I expect it to collapse.

I would structure the trade using options, selling far out-of-the-money calls to finance the purchase of near-the-money puts, while also selling two or three far out-of-the-money puts to reduce the cost further.

I would be happy to get assigned a short position in $UVXY if the short calls are exercised, as that would likely mean the $VIX has moved well above 30.

Position sizing is key here. Position sizing is also your risk management.
